distribution_frequency: Quarterly. ARCC pays a single regular quarterly dividend; no monthly and no supplemental/variable component was declared in any of the last four quarters (flat $0.48 for 12 consecutive quarters, 2024Q1-2026Q2, per the quarterly NAV/price/dividend table).

dividend_coverage_last4.return_of_capital_flag: No return-of-capital characterization is disclosed in this 10-Q. GAAP NII covered distributions in each of the last four quarters (2025Q3 exactly 1.00x).
dividend_coverage_last4.capital_gains_fee_reversal_caveat: GAAP NII is FLATTERED by the capital gains incentive fee reversal, which is a credit to expense driven by unrealized DEPRECIATION. Q2-2026 NII of $359mm includes a $(21)mm credit; Q1-2026 includes $(61)mm (6M $(82)mm less Q2 $(21)mm). Excluding the credit, NII/share would be ~$0.47 in each of 2026Q1 and 2026Q2 -- BELOW the $0.48 declared distribution. This is an observation from the face of the income statement, not an adjustment ARCC makes.

risk_rating_migration.scale: ARCC internal grades 1-4. DIRECTION VERIFIED FROM FILING TEXT: Grade 4 = "Involves the LEAST amount of risk to our initial cost basis"; Grade 1 = "risk ... has SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED ... portfolio company likely has materially declining performance". HIGHER GRADE = BETTER. This is the inverse of the common convention.
risk_rating_migration.direction: ADVERSE. The two worst buckets (grades 1+2) rose from 3.8% to 5.4% of portfolio fair value ($1,123mm -> $1,582mm, +40.9%) and from 52 to 61 companies. Grade 2 alone rose 61% in dollars ($675mm -> $1,089mm). Grade 3 fell from 79.1% to 77.1%. Weighted average grade unchanged at 3.1 (rounding masks the shift).
risk_rating_migration.comparison_basis: vs December 31, 2025 (the only comparative the 10-Q provides). MARCH 31, 2026 GRADE DISTRIBUTION IS NOT IN THIS FILING -- see coverage_gaps.

structural_notes.management: EXTERNALLY MANAGED by Ares Capital Management (an affiliate of Ares Management). Administration by Ares Operations. Either agreement terminable on 60 days notice.
structural_notes.base_management_fee: 1.5% annual on total assets (excluding cash/cash equivalents), REDUCED to 1.0% on assets financed using leverage above 1.0x debt-to-equity, effective 2019-06-21 in exchange for the 150% asset coverage election. Q2-2026 base fee $110mm.

income_based_fee.hurdle: 1.75% per quarter (7.0% annualized) on net assets, measured on PRE-incentive-fee net investment income.
income_based_fee.catch_up: 100% of pre-incentive-fee NII between the 1.75% hurdle and 2.1875% per quarter (the "catch-up"), designed to give the adviser 20% of all pre-incentive-fee NII once the 2.1875% level is reached.
income_based_fee.above_catch_up: 20% of pre-incentive-fee NII above 2.1875% per quarter.
income_based_fee.pik_inclusion: CRITICAL: pre-incentive-fee NII EXPLICITLY INCLUDES accrued-but-not-received income from deferred-income features -- PIK interest, PIK preferred dividends, market discount and zero-coupon accretion. The filing states the adviser "is not under any obligation to reimburse the Company for any part of the income based fee it received that were based on accrued income that the Company never actually received." With PIK at ~15.8% of total investment income, the adviser is paid on non-cash income with no clawback.
income_based_fee.loss_quarters: The filing states the income based fee is payable even in a quarter where ARCC incurs a loss from realized/unrealized capital losses.

capital_gains_incentive_fee.mechanics: 20% of cumulative aggregate realized capital gains less realized losses less aggregate unrealized depreciation, determined annually in arrears, less fees paid in prior years.
capital_gains_incentive_fee.gaap_vs_contractual: GAAP requires the accrual to also consider cumulative unrealized APPRECIATION. As of 2026-06-30 there was NO capital gains incentive fee actually payable under the agreement, and NO cumulatively accrued fee under GAAP.
capital_gains_incentive_fee.note: The negative amounts are REVERSALS of previously accrued GAAP expense, driven by the quarter's unrealized depreciation. They increase reported NII.

total_return_lookback_TRIGGERED.test: Cash payment of income based fee and capital gains incentive fee is DEFERRED if, over the most recent four full calendar quarters, the sum of (a) aggregate distributions to stockholders and (b) the change in net assets is LESS THAN 7.0% of net assets at the beginning of that period.
total_return_lookback_TRIGGERED.status: TRIGGERED THIS QUARTER. The filing states: "payment of the $84 income based fee earned by the Company's investment adviser for the second quarter of 2026 has been deferred." Disclosed in BOTH Note 3 and MD&A.
total_return_lookback_TRIGGERED.significance: The adviser's own total-return protection mechanism activated -- ARCC's trailing-four-quarter total return (distributions plus NAV change) fell below 7.0%. The fee is deferred, not waived: it carries over for payment in subsequent periods to the extent then payable.

NII PER SHARE FOR 2025Q3 AND 2025Q4 are DERIVED, not directly stated. Quarterly NII dollars come straight from primary filings ($338mm Q3-2025 from the Q3-2025 10-Q; $370mm Q4-2025 = FY2025 $1,415mm less 9M $1,045mm from the FY2025 10-K). Per-share figures are derived by differencing year-to-date weighted-average per-share amounts from the financial-highlights tables, which carries small error when the share count changes intra-year. Cross-checked against dollars/share counts: Q3-25 338/706=0.479, Q4-25 370/718=0.515, Q1-26 398/718=0.554, Q2-26 359/718=0.500. Both methods agree to a cent.

NON-ACCRUAL COUNT (22) is a derived count of PORTFOLIO COMPANIES carrying SOI footnote (8), not a figure ARCC states. ARCC gives only the 2.4%/1.4% percentages. My tranche-level recompute reproduces those percentages (2.38%/1.38%), which validates the footnote extraction.

PORTFOLIO COMPANY COUNT DEFINITION: my SOI parse yields 593 distinct borrower LINES; ARCC states 619 portfolio companies in the grade table. The difference is definitional -- the SOI presents co-borrower groups (e.g. "X Inc. and X Holdings LP") on a single line while the grade table counts companies. Dollar totals tie EXACTLY ($29,674.6mm cost / $29,349.3mm fair value vs the filing's own SOI total), so no dollars are lost; only the entity count differs.

BORROWER NAMES in top20 are verbatim from the SOI Company column with only the trailing footnote-reference markers removed (e.g. "(13)(14)"). Those markers are filing apparatus, not part of the name. Multi-entity borrower groups are preserved in full for cross-manager matching.
TOP-20 RANKING IS BY FAIR VALUE at the borrower-group level. ARCC does not publish a top-20 table; this is constructed from the full parsed SOI.
PIK for the SDLP and IHAM look-through is not separable: PIK earned INSIDE the SDLP and IHAM portfolios is not disclosed. ARCC's 15.8% PIK share reflects only PIK it receives directly.
